html:
A civil servant from the south who became president of Cameroon on 6 November 1982, when Ahmadou Ahidjo resigned, and has ruled ever since.

He survived a coup attempt in 1984, allowed multiparty politics in 1990 and won every election since, often amid charges of fraud. In 2008 term limits were removed. Cameroon has stayed fairly stable, but corruption is high, and his long stays abroad are well known. His government's hard response to protests in the English-speaking regions led to the Anglophone Crisis, and the north has faced Boko Haram. He was declared the winner again in 2025, at 92, amid protests. See also Cameroon.
